function: CSI feedback: autoencoder (CRNet) compresses and reconstructs the angular-delay CSI matrix, trained with data augmentation against the train-test delay gap (p. 2, p. 4).
system: Single-cell FDD massive MIMO, 32-antenna ULA at the BS, one UE antenna, 1024 subcarriers; indoor 5.3 GHz, outdoor 300 MHz; no RIS (p. 2, p. 4).
method: CRNet autoencoder with multi-resolution convolutions, supervised on augmented CSI; bubble-shift circularly shifts amplitude columns, random-generation adds random k-by-k blocks (p. 1, p. 3, p. 4).
data_channel: COST 2100 simulated CSI, indoor 5.3 GHz and outdoor 300 MHz; 50,000 training samples (100,000 after augmentation), 10,000 test samples (p. 4).
test_conditions: Train: farthest vertical path; test: any vertical path. Or train: 10m indoor, 200m outdoor squares; test: 40m, 800m squares (p. 4).
baselines: No augmentation, RPS [10], flipping [9], JPTS [8], and model-driven shifting [7], all applied to CRNet; no non-learned CSI feedback method compared (p. 4).
metrics: NMSE in dB at compression rates 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32, 1/64, indoor and outdoor; MSE loss curves of training and test (p. 4, p. 5).
openness: Datasets released at https://github.com/zhanghy23/CRNet-Aug/ (p. 1, p. 2); code not mentioned.
q1_support: p. 4: "We use COST2100 [12] to generate the data in the indoor environment at 5.3GHz and outdoor environment at 300MHz."
q2_support: p. 4: "we set UEs in the training dataset to move at the farthest vertical path away from the BS. UEs in the testing dataset can move at any vertical path"; the motion-range scenario widens the area from 10m to 40m indoor and 200m to 800m outdoor.
q3_support: p. 4: "All the augmentation approaches are tested with the CRNet structure to have a fair comparison"; every baseline (No Aug, RPS, Flip, JPTS, M-D) trains CRNet, and no non-learned CSI feedback method such as compressed sensing (only named on p. 1) is compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "The number of samples in the training dataset is 50,000 and turns to 100,000 after offline augmentation"; this is dataset size only, with no FLOPs, parameters, runtime, or complexity order of B-S, R-G, or CRNet anywhere.
q5_support: p. 1: "The open-source datasets are available at https://github.com/zhanghy23/" followed on the next line by CRNet-Aug/ (link repeated on p. 2); the data are COST 2100 simulations released with a link.
notes: Included as CSI feedback (area 2): the contribution is a training-data augmentation (bubble-shift, random-generation) for autoencoder CSI feedback, evaluated on CRNet. q2 rests on the explicit train-test gap in UE motion mode and motion range. q3 is 0 because no non-learned feedback method is compared. The GitHub link appears on p. 1 and, split across a line break, on p. 2.
